Any point on line $\frac{x-4}{1}=\frac{y-9}{2}=\frac{z-5}{1}$: $(4+t,9+2t,5+t)$.
Foot $(1,\mu,2)$: $4+t=1\Rightarrow t=-3$, so $\mu=3$, $z=2$ ✓. Foot $=(1,3,2)$.
Perpendicularity with direction $(1,2,1)$: $(\lambda-1)+2(2-3)+(3-2)=0\Rightarrow\lambda=2$.
Both lines have direction $\vec b=(2,3,6)$, so they are parallel.
Points: $A(1,2,-4)$, $B(2,3,-5)$; $\vec{AB}=(1,1,-1)$, $|\vec b|=7$.
Distance between parallel lines: $d=\frac{|\vec{AB}\times\vec b|}{|\vec b|}$.
$\vec{AB}\times\vec b=(1\cdot6+1\cdot3,\,-2-6,\,3-2)=(9,-8,1)$, magnitude $\sqrt{146}$.
$d=\frac{\sqrt{146}}{7}$
Answer: (C) $\frac{\sqrt{146}}{7}$
